## Overview

Canvas-Risk is a terminal dashboard that connects to the Canvas LMS API and flags students who are at risk of falling behind — missing work, slipping grades, and inactivity — before it's too late in the semester to fix. It touches every layer of the stack: an external API client, a persistent database, an analytics engine on top, and an interactive UI.

**Stack:** Python, SQLAlchemy, SQLite, Textual, Typer

## Architecture

| Layer | Role |
|---|---|
| `api/` | Paginated client that pulls students, assignments, and submissions from the Canvas REST API |
| `database/` | SQLAlchemy models + a SQLite manager for local caching and historical trend tracking |
| `analytics/` | The risk-scoring engine |
| `ui/` | A real-time Textual dashboard |
| `commands/` | Typer-based CLI for quick terminal reports |

## The Risk Engine

Each student's failure probability is a weighted blend of signals pulled straight from the synced Canvas data — current grade, missing assignments, grade trend over time, inactivity, and how they compare to their peers:

```python
WEIGHTS = {
    'grade': 0.40,
    'missing': 0.30,
    'trend': 0.10,
    'inactivity': 0.10,
    'peer_comparison': 0.10
}
```

On top of the raw score, students get tagged into a profile — High Achiever, The Ghost (inactive with missing work), Slipping, Chronic Latecomer, and so on — so a TA scanning the dashboard gets an instant read instead of just a number.

## Why It Matters

This is the project that best represents "full stack" for me: real external data in, a proper local data model, analysis logic that turns raw numbers into a decision-ready signal, and a UI that makes it usable without touching a database client. Every layer had to work for the last one to mean anything.
